findings.claim: The repair-installed citation of the row's tier-1 address anchor is worded as a negative ('stands unused'), directly contradicting the citation's own evidentiary purpose: the defect this repair was ordered to cure was precisely that the anchor went uncited, and the installed prose still asserts the anchor is unused even while now citing it.
findings.evidence: span Song.1.8-Song.1.11; boundary_rationale (verbatim, full field; the repair-installed anchor citation is the middle sentence containing 'stands unused'): "אִם לֹ֤א תֵדְעִי֙ (oshb:Song.1.8, tier: byte) opens this unit: the negation sits on אִם לֹ֤א ('if not'), and תֵדְעִי֙ itself carries second-feminine-singular marking ('you know') rather than the opening token, a grammatical-gender flip from the second-masculine address of Song.1.7 that signals a new speaker. The feminine imperatives צְֽאִי and וּרְעִי֙ (oshb:Song.1.8, tier: byte, 'go out' / 'graze') hold one addressee (her); inside the span's own bytes, רַעְיָתִֽי (oshb:Song.1.9, tier: byte, 'my love'), his tier-1 address anchor for her (sweep: 9 verses), stands unused alongside the 2fs object suffix on דִּמִּיתִ֖יךְ (oshb:Song.1.9, tier: byte, 'I have compared you'). The second-feminine-singular suffixes continue through לְחָיַ֨יִךְ֙ (oshb:Song.1.10, tier: byte, 'your cheeks') and לָּ֔ךְ (oshb:Song.1.11, tier: byte, the 2fs dative in 'we will make for you'), holding one addressee across all four verses with no further gender-marked interruption: “Your cheeks are beautiful with earrings, your neck with strings of jewels.” (web:Song.1.10) and “We will make you earrings of gold, with studs of silver.” (web:Song.1.11)." The c01_PEER/OL work order (SP/Song/work_orders.json) ordered exactly this splice 'as the span's tier-1 address anchor' to cure the finding that 'the row neither argues MT 1:9 in prose nor mirrors it into boundary_evidence_refs, and it is the single strongest available warrant for the row's own male-voice reading.' The repair added oshb:Song.1.9 to boundary_evidence_refs (present in rows_v2.jsonl, absent from draft_rows_combined.jsonl), yet the installed prose still labels the anchor 'unused' -- a self-undermining warrant installed by the repair itself.

findings.claim: The row's repair-installed device_notes sentence contains erratum/repair-history narration ('undisclosed until now') describing the row's own disclosure state across drafts rather than making a textual claim about the verses -- barred under the standing REGISTER PURGE rule.
findings.evidence: span Song.2.16-Song.2.17; device_notes (verbatim, full field; the repair-installed segment ends '...undisclosed until now.'): "The ad-she-yafuach-ha-yom closing formula, עַ֤ד שֶׁיָּפ֨וּחַ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם וְנָ֖סוּ הַצְּלָלִ֑ים (oshb:Song.2.17, tier: byte), recurs once more character-identical at oshb:Song.4.6 (tier: byte; sweep: 2 verses). The gazelle-and-fawn colon at Song.2.17 shares a consonantal run at skeleton tier with the same colon back at Song.2.9 and forward at Song.8.14 (sweep: 3 verses: MT 2:9, 2:17, 8:14), undisclosed until now. Song.2.17 carries a setumah in the WLC (single-witness, tier-3 corroboration only) at this unit's own close." This sentence is absent from both draft_rows_combined.jsonl and rows_v1.jsonl for this row. TOOLKIT.md 'Standing rules' bars 'erratum narration, positional row references, file-order talk' from row prose 'EVER'; 'undisclosed until now' narrates the row's own before/after disclosure history rather than describing the biblical text.

findings.claim: The same row's repair-installed boundary_rationale sentence names the internal peer-review cluster grouping ('in this cluster') instead of a verse-anchored reference, reproducing the reviewer's own internal grounds language almost verbatim rather than rewriting it into row-appropriate prose.
findings.evidence: span Song.2.16-Song.2.17; boundary_rationale (verbatim, full field; repair-installed segment ends '...drives the cut at Song.2.15 in this cluster.'): "דּוֹדִ֥י לִי֙ וַאֲנִ֣י ל֔וֹ (oshb:Song.2.16, tier: byte, 'my beloved is mine, and I am his') is the first of three attested mutual-belonging shapes in the book (sweep: 3 verses), in the his-mine order; Song.2.17 continues in the same first-person voice, held as tier-2 single-speaker corroboration alongside the mutual-belonging formula site rather than on any addressee-free ground. Within Song.2.17 itself the address turns second-masculine-singular: סֹב֩ דְּמֵה לְךָ֨ דוֹדִ֜י (oshb:Song.2.17, tier: byte, 'turn, be like, my beloved'), the final-kaf-plus-qamats suffix on לְךָ֨ contrasting with the final-kaf-plus-sheva second-feminine-singular suffix on מַרְאַ֔יִךְ (oshb:Song.2.14, tier: byte, 'your face'); the unit's own texture therefore carries an addressed imperative, not an interruption-free run, and the same feature drives the cut at Song.2.15 in this cluster. The unit closes on “Until the day is cool, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be like a roe or a young deer on the mountains of Bether.” (web:Song.2.17)." Compare SP/Song/work_orders.json c02_PEER/OL grounds for this same row (verbatim): '...and the same feature drives a cut at Song.2.15 in this cluster, so the criterion is applied inconsistently.' The installed row prose imports the reviewer's internal-grouping phrase ('in this cluster', i.e. the c02 peer-review cluster) directly from the work-order grounds text instead of a verse-anchored formulation; TOOLKIT.md requires 'Cross-row references are verse-anchored' and bars 'file-order talk' from row prose.

findings.claim: The row's strongest_rejected_alternative asserts an unswept, unlocated superlative ('the book's one true imperative') for a morphological claim the toolkit explicitly states cannot be machine-verified from the staged extract -- a class-1 unswept-universal defect surviving in the one field this repair otherwise carefully tier-labeled and digit-swept.
findings.evidence: span Song.4.1-Song.4.7; strongest_rejected_alternative (verbatim, full field): "Extending the wasf through Song.4.8 was rejected: תָּב֑וֹאִי (oshb:Song.4.8, tier: byte) is a prefix-conjugation form of the same root as the book's one true imperative, not an imperative itself, but כַּלָּ֔ה (oshb:Song.4.8, tier: byte), the bride-epithet's first site (sweep: 6 verses, word-bound), still marks a new invitational unit distinct from the body-part inclusio closed at Song.4.7." No verse citation or sweep digit accompanies the 'one true imperative' claim anywhere in the row (the c03_PEER/OL work-order grounds locate the real 2fs imperative at oshb:Song.4.16, but that location is never spliced into this row). TOOLKIT.md states 'NO MORPHOLOGY LAYER in the staged extract...Form claims (gender of a suffix or verb, jussive, participle) CANNOT be machine-verified with the staged tools' -- an unlocated 'sole' claim about verb-form uniqueness is exactly the class-1 hazard (a sole/first/last-type claim with no adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming object+unit).
